title: (close #7276) spec: does `string` have a `Dispose()` METHOD (a no-op), or not?  --  8.7/14.2 vs 28.2 clause 6
body:
Spec v0.345 ({{SHA}}, on the review branch, not yet on `main`), decided as a delegated ruling under the owner's 2026-10-08 direction ("Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them.") and the 2026-10-27 direction for this train ("Post the rulings including on 7276, consider whether any clarifications are needed in the spec, and do a new train to resolve known spec issues. Don't land it on main yet though, but work on a separate branch."). **Option 3, by proposal 0200 (`docs/proposals/0200-dispose-member-only-on-disposable-types.md`) (design change).** `string` has **no `Dispose()` member**, and neither have `Type`, boxed values or function values. `Dispose()` is a member of class types, of the interfaces that are or extend `IDisposable` (the set `where T: IDisposable` admits) and of an interface declaring `method Dispose();` itself (§28.2); `DisposeAsync()` of the types that declare or inherit it; neither of anything else (§8.7). `s.Dispose()` is a compile error at the type level — the reason `Object` already gets (#6990) — and a `using var`, a discard or scope end over a string stays admitted and disposes nothing (§28.9). A generic body under `where T: class` alone has no `Dispose()` on `T` (constrain to `IDisposable`, or use the discard); an extension block may not declare a member named `Dispose` or `DisposeAsync` (§26.3). `string` is not a class (§3.5 and stdlib §9.6 reworded).

**Why no member, not a no-op:** a no-op `Dispose()` claims a kill it does not perform, could not be an `IDisposable` implementation (§28.1 clause 6), and could not be written legally anyway, since §28.6 requires an owned receiver and a runtime-managed value is never owned (K1.6). Marking a string disposed is unsound: strings are shared by assignment, may be interned, and cross domains as shared references. Both are `declined-at-proposal` rows, with an implicit `Dispose()` on every interface type (#7068's option 2).

**Compiler:** [#7273](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/7273) is the tracker (retitled, `spec-tracking`). Measured reach of the string half: 0 sites; the interface and `where T: class` halves flip 23 gtest rows and re-cut one lit row (the proposal's §6). The function-value arm already landed with [#7260](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/7260)'s narrowing fix.
